readme:
# Amazon Jobs Scraper

Scrapes job listings from [Amazon Jobs](https://www.amazon.jobs). Each row has the title, team and category, every location, the posting date, the full description, the basic and preferred qualifications and the apply link, ready for a spreadsheet, a database or an AI agent.

## What you can do with it

- Search by one or more keywords, or leave the keywords empty to list all open jobs.
- Narrow the search by country, location and job category.
- Get the newest postings first (`sortBy: recent`, the default), or sort by relevance.
- Keep only recent postings with `postedWithinDays`.
- Paste Amazon Jobs search pages or single job pages into `startUrls`. Tracking parameters such as `utm_source` are ignored.
- Run it on a schedule to build a daily feed of new Amazon jobs.

## Input

| Field | Meaning | Default |
|-------|---------|---------|
| `searchQueries` | Keywords, one search each. Empty means all jobs. | all jobs |
| `location` | Cities, regions or countries, for example `Seattle`, `Texas`, `Germany`, `Berlin, Germany` | all locations |
| `country` | Country names or codes (`Germany`, `DE`, `DEU`) | all countries |
| `category` | Job categories, for example `Software Development` | all categories |
| `sortBy` | `recent` or `relevant` | `recent` |
| `postedWithinDays` | Only jobs posted in the last N days, 0 or empty = no filter | no filter |
| `maxResultsPerQuery` | Cap per keyword, location and start URL | 10 |
| `maxResults` | Cap across all searches, empty = no total cap | no total cap |
| `startUrls` | Amazon Jobs search or job page URLs | none |

An empty input (`{}`) runs a small demo that returns the 5 newest jobs, so you can see the output format.

Each search returns at most 10,000 jobs, so split very large pulls by country or category.

Examples:

```json
{
  "searchQueries": ["data scientist", "solutions architect"],
  "country": ["Germany", "United Kingdom"],
  "sortBy": "recent",
  "postedWithinDays": 14,
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 100
}
```

```json
{
  "category": ["Software Development"],
  "location": ["Seattle, Washington, USA"],
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 200
}
```

```json
{
  "startUrls": [
    "https://www.amazon.jobs/en/search?base_query=python&country=DEU",
    "https://www.amazon.jobs/en/jobs/10588363/head-operations"
  ],
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 50
}
```

### Supported URLs

| URL | What you get |
|-----|--------------|
| `https://www.amazon.jobs/en/search?base_query=python&country=DEU` | Jobs of that search, with its keyword, country, category and location filters |
| `https://www.amazon.jobs/en/jobs/10588363/head-operations` | That one job |
| `https://www.amazon.jobs/en/search` | All jobs, newest first |

## Output

One row per job. Missing values are `null` (or an empty list), never an empty string.

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `id` | Internal Amazon posting id (UUID) |
| `job_id` | The Job ID shown on the job page, unique per posting |
| `title` | Job title |
| `job_url`, `source_url` | Public job page |
| `source_platform` | `amazon.jobs` |
| `apply_url` | Link to apply |
| `company_name` | Hiring Amazon company |
| `business_category` | Business area, for example `retail` or `aws` |
| `job_category`, `job_family` | Category and family as the site lists them |
| `team`, `team_slug` | Team, when the posting names one |
| `job_schedule_type` | For example `full-time` |
| `is_intern` | Best-effort flag derived from the title and the team: `true` when the title or team names an internship or the team is a student program, otherwise `false`. The site has no such field, so check edge cases yourself |
| `location`, `normalized_location`, `city` | Primary location |
| `state_code`, `state` | State or province code (`WA`) and full name (`Washington`) of the primary location |
| `country_code`, `country_code_iso2`, `country` | Country of the primary location |
| `all_locations` | Every location of the job: city, state, country, type, latitude, longitude, building codes |
| `posted_at` | Posting date (ISO date) |
| `updated_time` | How long ago the posting was updated, as the site shows it |
| `description`, `description_html` | Full description as text and as HTML |
| `basic_qualifications`, `basic_qualifications_html` | Basic qualifications |
| `preferred_qualifications`, `preferred_qualifications_html` | Preferred qualifications, `null` when the posting has none |
| `search_query` | The keyword that found the job (`null` without a keyword or for job URLs) |
| `scraped_at` | When the row was collected (UTC) |

Sample row (long texts shortened):

```json
{
  "id": "d246900d-df77-4ca9-92c0-14cc81e498ea",
  "job_id": "10587034",
  "title": "Principal Applied Scientist, AWS Data Center Services",
  "job_url": "https://www.amazon.jobs/en/jobs/10587034/principal-applied-scientist-aws-data-center-services",
  "apply_url": "https://account.amazon.jobs/jobs/10587034/apply",
  "company_name": "Amazon Data Services, Inc.",
  "business_category": "aws",
  "job_category": "Applied Science",
  "job_family": "Applied Science",
  "team": "Machine learning",
  "job_schedule_type": "full-time",
  "is_intern": false,
  "normalized_location": "Seattle, Washington, USA",
  "city": "Seattle",
  "state_code": "WA",
  "state": "Washington",
  "country_code": "USA",
  "country": "United States",
  "posted_at": "2026-10-22",
  "updated_time": "2 days",
  "description": "Application deadline: Oct 27, 2026 ...",
  "basic_qualifications": "PhD in Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Statistics or in a highly quantitative field. ...",
  "search_query": "data scientist",
  "scraped_at": "2026-10-26T08:39:47Z"
}
```

## Pricing

This Actor uses pay-per-event pricing:

- `job-result`: one event for every job row that lands in the dataset. Duplicates across searches are removed first and are not charged.
- `apify-actor-start`: one event per run.

That is $1.00 per 1,000 jobs + $0.001 per run start. The description and qualifications come with every job at no extra charge. If you set a maximum charge per run, the Actor stops when the next job would exceed it and reports how many jobs were delivered.

Every Apify account includes a monthly free credit, which is enough to try the Actor on real searches.

## Use with AI agents (MCP)

Connect this Actor to any MCP-compatible AI client through the Apify MCP server:

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/amazon-jobs-scraper
```

Example prompt once connected: "Use amazon-jobs-scraper to list the newest software development jobs at Amazon in Germany posted in the last 7 days, with their basic qualifications."

## FAQ

**How do I find the URL of a search?** Open Amazon Jobs in your browser, set the keyword and filters you want, and copy the address bar into `startUrls`. Or skip URLs and use `searchQueries`, `country`, `location` and `category`.

**Why is a field empty?** Amazon does not fill every field for every posting. `team` is only set when the posting names a team, `preferred_qualifications` is empty for some roles, and `state_code` and `state` are empty in countries without states.

**How do I get only new jobs?** Schedule the Actor with `sortBy: recent` and `postedWithinDays: 1` (or 2 for an overlap). Use `job_id` to de-duplicate against earlier runs.

**How do I stop at a budget?** Set `maxResults`, or the maximum charge per run in the run options. At $1.00 per 1,000 jobs, 500 jobs cost about $0.50.

**Why does a job show a different city than the one I searched?** Many jobs are posted for several cities. `city` is the first one, `all_locations` lists them all.
